The C6 adapter implements the engine's platform ports (MonotonicClock, RunnerWait, WakeSignal, HardwareWatchdog) and its process-image port over esp-hal; the shared no_std crate resolves for the chip build and for the host build of its USB FIFO servicing (usb_service, tests/usb_service.rs).

allowed_workspace_edges.owner: runtime portability C1 (memory figures, spec 34 MEM-12)
allowed_workspace_edges.rationale: The heap test enables the core's footprint feature to drop a prepared module part by part and attribute its heap; a dev edge only, so no firmware build enables the measurement.

The C6 adapter implements the runner's ProcessIo port over esp-hal, reports its driver health through the shared status records, and moves its USB control port's bytes through the shared line link; the shared no_std crate resolves for the chip build and for the host build of its USB FIFO servicing (usb_service, tests/usb_service.rs).

The C6 adapter keeps the shared fixed-size reset record in persistent RTC fast memory and re-exports its cause and record types; the bare-metal memory crate holds the record codec and depends on no runtime or compiler.

allowed_workspace_edges.owner: runtime portability M2E (shared fixture and C6)
allowed_workspace_edges.rationale: Separate firmware workspace composes the fixed C6 board peripheral adapter.

The hosted runtime composes the shared no_std runtime services (spec 34 ARCH-11, ARCH-14) and re-exports the control envelope and access rights at their existing paths; transports, threads and host state stay in trust-runtime.

The shared runtime services use the engine's records (resource state, restart mode, watchdog and fault policies, durations, runtime errors and the libm rounding primitive) through the core built without std; the core never depends on the services (forbidden edge).

The shared chip platform (chip::platform) reads the fixed-size reset record a chip keeps across a reset into the capabilities reply, so the C6 and the STM32U5A9 report the same cause from one copy of the mapping; the memory crate holds the record codec and depends on no runtime or compiler.
The panel engine reads trust-runtime's wire types, configuration, catalog and control glue; it is a host tool and no chip links it.
The panel engine reaches runtimes through the one shared control client.
The panel shows a runtime whose status names a chip of truST's chip files as that chip; the reader depends on no firmware or adapter.
The five `trust-lsp.devices*` commands decode their arguments, run the panel engine on a blocking thread and return its JSON (design §1.4.1 and §1.6).
The engine integration test drives the panel engine against a real `trust-runtime` binary; a dev edge only, so no runtime or firmware build resolves the reader.
trust-runtime firmware install places each part of a chip's firmware where the chip file's layout puts it (specification 34 TARGET-03, TARGET-04); the reader depends on no firmware or adapter.
trust-runtime discover reaches the runtime that runs a search through the one shared control client; the client depends on no truST crate.
The STM32U5A9 adapter uses the shared STM32 rules for its pin names and its pin table lookup; the shared crate depends on nothing.
A host test compares the STM32U5A9 chip table and its clock with chips/stm32u5a9.toml; a dev edge only, so no firmware build resolves the reader.
The STM32U5A9 control link implements the engine's ControlLink, MonotonicClock and WakeSignal ports; the core depends on no platform crate.
The control link carries the shared line link of the runtime services (framing, reply and stall rule), as the C6 adapter does; the services depend on no platform crate.

The STM32U5A9 memory map gives the shared measurement crate its main-stack window, and its reset store implements the shared ResetStore; the memory crate holds the record codec and depends on no runtime or compiler.
The program library is compiled into every program module together with the kernel interface whose cells, strings and faults its functions use (specification 44 §6.9).

The kernel fills the context of the module interface and calls a compiled program's entry points through it (specification 44 §8.2, §8.3); the interface crate has no dependencies and builds on every chip.
The build lays out compiled programs against the module interface and the computer's kernel maps a module's code executable through its host side (specification 44 §4, §10.3).
The build lays out the standard function blocks at the program library's own offsets, which every module links (specification 44 §6.8).
The C6 calls a compiled program's module where its image lies in the mapped slot, through the interface's in-place code (specification 44 §10.3).
The compiled cycle's tests run stand-in modules written against the kernel interface; a dev edge only, so the shared services never depend on it.

module_size_allowlist.split_plan: Keep one child module per driver and split a driver's own module by responsibility (parameters, point maps, request plan, exchange, protocol codec) before any file approaches 1000 lines; the shared parameter reader stays in io_drivers.rs.

module_size_allowlist.rationale: Spec 44 groups the kernel's side of compiled programs: the program image's reader, writer and records, the deployment record of an image, the kernel's program (admission, areas, scan, bindings, faults), the Live Values bindings and the retained variables through the retain map. Each is a real child module with its tests beside it; the aggregate is not one large implementation file or a mixed owner.
module_size_allowlist.split_plan: Keep the image format in native/image.rs with its records and writer, the record in native/record.rs, the program in native/program.rs, the Live Values bindings in native/live.rs and the retained variables in native/retain.rs. Split any individual file approaching 1000 lines by its existing responsibility; the copy plan of an online change and the debugger's symbol access (milestone M3) get their own child modules.

module_size_allowlist.rationale: The shared debug operations of every runtime: the breakpoint record and its hit rule, the run control, the statement identity, the line sources, the request parsing, the reply shapes, the variable projection and its pages, and the reads of the interpreter's held state and of a compiled program's memory. Each is a real child module with its own tests beside it; the aggregate's size comes from those tests and from two read paths (the interpreter's and the compiled program's), not from one large implementation file or a mixed owner.
module_size_allowlist.split_plan: Keep requests.rs, replies.rs, reads.rs, compiled.rs, projection.rs, paging.rs, sources.rs, run.rs, breakpoint.rs and statement.rs on their own responsibilities. The interpreter's read path (reads.rs and its VariableStorage projection in projection.rs) goes with the bytecode engine at the one list's N11, which brings the module under the threshold; split any file approaching 1000 lines, a test file included, by the rules it pins.

module_size_allowlist.rationale: The device runner namespace is the resource loop and one contract test file per port: the loop and its link/wait boundary, the cycle port, the shared-engine cycle with its limits, process I/O and services, the program wrapper, the platform host, the supervisor, the records and the retain store. Slice C5-3b added the chip retention contract tests (runner/retain_contract_tests.rs) beside the loop they exercise, which takes the aggregate past 5000 lines; the boundary is the sum of focused files, not one implementation file or a mixed owner.
module_size_allowlist.split_plan: Keep one responsibility per child file: the loop, the cycle port, the shared-engine cycle, the platform host, the supervisor, the records and the retain store stay separate, and each port's contract tests stay beside the loop they exercise. Split any individual file approaching 1000 lines by the same responsibility rather than growing runner.rs.

module_size_allowlist.rationale: The view namespace is the panel contract of specification 25 §5.15 and its projection, in focused child modules: the contract types (split into vocabulary, graph and panes), health rules, computers, runtimes, lifecycle actions, the list, connections, devices and links, the filter and search, issues, status reading and addresses, with their tests and golden scenarios beside them. The pane builders (add dialog, forms, USB tray) live in the sibling `panes` namespace and answer the pane types of this contract. No single file or mixed owner; about a third of the lines are tests.
module_size_allowlist.split_plan: Keep one child module per panel concern; B5 added connections, devices, links, search and issues as their own files. The panes now live in the sibling `panes` namespace beside `view` (add dialog, forms, USB tray; later Discover and browse), and new panes go there; their contract types stay in `view/types/panes.rs`. Split any file approaching 1000 lines by its responsibility.

module_size_allowlist.rationale: The panel's action path of specification 25 §5.4, §5.9, §5.13 and §5.14, in focused child modules: the closed action set and its dispatch, the host-effect lists, the forms and connection actions, the connection plans, the ADS route action, the runtime actions, and the one write path they share, each with its tests beside it. No single file or mixed owner; about half the lines are tests.
module_size_allowlist.split_plan: Keep one child module per action family; B7 added `ads.rs` for the browse pane's `Create route` beside the plans. Split any file approaching 1000 lines by its responsibility, and put a new action family in its own child module.

module_size_allowlist.rationale: The panes beside the graph of specification 25 §2 and §5.12-§5.14, in focused child modules: the add dialog, the forms, the USB tray, and the browse panes (OPC UA nodes, EtherCAT channels, exposed globals and, with B8b1, the ADS tag browser in `browse/ads.rs`), each with its tests beside it. The aggregate crosses 5000 lines as the sum of these focused modules; no single file is near 1000 lines and about a third of the lines are tests.
module_size_allowlist.split_plan: Keep one child module per pane concern; the browse panes keep one child per protocol family under `browse/`. Split any file approaching 1000 lines by its own responsibility.
